description: Committee recommends naming Saskatoon Field House track Lyle Sanderson.
This allows an exception to interior facility naming policy.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Jeffries argued both commemorative and corporate naming could coexist.
Administration noted potential $27,500 annual revenue loss from naming rights.
Administration recommended against naming due to lost sponsorship revenue.
Naming the track could set a precedent for future interior facility requests.
Delegates highlighted Lyle Sanderson's national contributions to track and field.

speakers.name: Krista Bowles
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Lyle Sanderson Naming Proposal
said: Saskatoon names facilities for shining stars whose influence shapes the community.
Lyle Sanderson's legacy inspired athletes, coaches, volunteers, and generations.
His gift was inspiring others to believe in his vision and make it their own.

speakers.name: Dale Yellowlees
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Lyle Sanderson Naming Proposal - Saskatoon Field House Track
said: Saskatoon has a history of naming sports facilities after deserving individuals.
Lyle Sanderson's career is one of the most deserving, with national and international success.
He pioneered the Field House's use, making it a hub for track and field.

description: Increase smoking setback distance from 3 to 10 metres.
Apply smoking restrictions to parking patios, medical marijuana.
Repeal outdated 1989 No Smoking Policy C06-001.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor thanked staff for detailed review, aligning Saskatoon with modern cities.
Implementation of changes suggested for January 1, 2027.

description: Committee recommends funding three heritage committee members.
Up to $10,500 for 2026 National Trust Conference attendance.
Funds from existing Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee budget.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Jeffries moved to approve $10,500 from existing MHAC budgets.

description: Replaces mandatory drainage plans with commitment letters.
Simplifies building permits, reduces costs for infill.
Changes would take effect January 1, 2027.

chips.text: Recommended
Mayor Block opposed shifting drainage burden to existing neighbors.
Residents adjacent to infill developments, like Nutana, are directly affected.
Administration seeks efficiency; councillors prioritize resident protection and cost recovery.
Questions raised on how commitment letters improve timelines or reduce costs.
Public delegates strongly opposed relaxing drainage requirements for infill.
Potential for bureaucratic issues and legal disputes flagged by delegate.
Administration will report back on cost recovery options for drainage enforcement.

speakers.name: Margaret Tompson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Drainage Bylaw
said: Proposed changes weaken bylaw, increasing infill drainage complaints.
Owners lack building experience to attest to drainage compliance.
Extending final inspection to 24 months magnifies drainage problems.

speakers.name: Robert Clipperton
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Amendments to Bylaw 9772, The Drainage Bylaw
said: Current bylaw reduced drainage complaints; relaxing requirements is unwise.
No community consultation occurred regarding proposed changes.
Proposed 24-month grace period creates bureaucratic nightmares and risks.

description: Removes an unused 2009 bylaw and a 1993 development appeals policy.
This cleanup does not affect current appeal processes.

chips.text: Recommended
City Solicitor clarified appeal decisions are delegated to the City Manager.
Question raised about monitoring development appeal decisions after policy repeal.
Public speaker Margaret Tompson expressed concern about lack of oversight for appeal decisions.

speakers.name: Margaret Tompson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Repeal of Bylaw No. 8757 and policy No. C09-007
said: City planners should report decisions that need to be appealed.
Current appeal hearings favor developers, not a level playing field.
City representative needs a mandate to alert council for appeals.

description: Council defers removing 25 downtown benches until September 2027.
City will evaluate downtown public amenities and maintenance programs.
City will explore a dedicated reporting line for businesses.

chips.text: Administration stated removing benches does not stop social disorder, it just moves it.
Seniors, children, and people with mobility limitations use downtown benches.
Council deferred administration's proposed temporary bench removal trial.
Councillor Jeffries' request for details on peer-reviewed research was not answered.
Downtown BID strongly supported temporary bench removal due to disorder and safety concerns.
Councillor Timon raised concerns about the equity and accessibility of removing benches.

description: Saskatoon Soccer Inc. plans to expand the Sports Centre.
Expansion is fully funded by Saskatoon Soccer Inc.
Adds 58 hours weekly of prime indoor turf.

chips.text: Councillor Buck highlighted urgent need for expansion due to soccer's popularity and affordability.
Youth soccer leagues and other users face programming challenges due to turf shortages.
Saskatoon Soccer CEO Jodi Blackwell presented the expansion plan, citing growing demand.

speakers.name: Jodi Blackwell
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Request to Expand Saskatoon Sports Centre
said: Growing demand for training times and quality facilities.
Expansion with artificial turf addresses gaps for youth soccer.
Seeks support to move forward with the expansion project.

description: City reviews how community grants are distributed to local groups.
Administration plans to formalize culture grants for multi-year funding.
No income-based assessment exists for youth sports subsidies.

chips.text: Councillor Parker questioned the report's analysis of income levels for sports grants.
Ukrainian Museum and Shakespeare on Saskatchewan advocated for formalizing culture grants.
Youth sports subsidy lacks income lens, preventing assessment of equity impact.
Administration will formalize the culture grant program into city policy.
